text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A demonstrator is injured as police break up a protest march over the mysterious death of student leader Solomon Muruli.
- A former university don urges the government to re-examine the quota system of admission to secondary schools as it promotes disparity in education.

- Willy Mutunga, executive director of the Citizens Coalition for Constitutional Change, asks Kenyans not to boycott the general elections even if the government does not allow for constitutional reforms.
- United States and British envoys condemn the mysterious death of student leader Solomon Muruli.
- Nine passengers burn to death after their vehicle collides with a trailer along the Eldoret-Nakuru highway.
- Angry Moslems opposed to the construction of a golf course on a disputed mosque plot destroy property worth thousands of shillings at Leisure Lodge hotel, Mombasa.
- Three parliamentarians and five police officers are interrogated over the death of Solomon Muruli.
- Energy permanent secretary Crispus Mutitu says oil companies should reduce pump prices for oil products in response to a fall in crude oil prices and a stable shilling.
- Nairobi provincial commissioner warns against violence at the coming Langata constituency by-election campaigns.
